Maintenance aims for safety, fewer defects, longer life, and lower downtime losses and costs. Combine scheduled service, monitoring, and repair; do not always run cheap parts until failure.

The textbook narrowly distinguishes hozen and hoshu, but workplace and standard usage can include inspection and prevention within hoshu too. A name alone does not determine safety or responsibility; check actual work, stopping conditions, and restart criteria.

mfg1-electrical-l082.title: Packaging marks, stacking, and PPM
mfg1-electrical-l082.exampleText: PPM expresses a count ratio per million.2 events in 10000 shipments is 2/10000×1000000=200 PPM. Do not fix acceptance values by industry or warehouse type alone; align customer target, population, period, and counting rules. Also assess timing, item, quantity, and destination.
mfg1-electrical-l082.structureTitle: Protection and distribution · Apply handling marks
mfg1-electrical-l082.structureText:
Match packaging to shock, vibration, humidity, storage duration, and product shape. Cushioning and restraints have different roles. Select paper, cardboard, wood, metal, or resin for the purpose; the outer box’s appearance does not guarantee internal protection.

Distinguish fragile, keep dry, handle with care, do not stack, and stacking-count limits. In the textbook, n is the number allowed above the bottom package; verify actual labels and packaging specifications. Do not rewrite marks yourself to permit overloading.

mfg1-electrical-l083.title: Injection molds, demolding, and FRP
mfg1-electrical-l083.exampleText: Thermoplastic, thermosetting, and biodegradable classifications differ in properties and treatment conditions. FRP’s mechanical and electrical behavior changes with glass/carbon fiber type, direction, and amount. Check strength, weight, chemical resistance, flammability, surface damage, disposal, and recycling against product specifications; not all FRP is identical.
mfg1-electrical-l083.structureTitle: The resin path · Remove the shape and store safely
mfg1-electrical-l083.structureText:
Injection molding feeds material from a hopper through a heated barrel and screw, then sprue, runner, and gate to the product cavity. Clamping holds the mold against injection pressure. Manage temperature, pressure, quantity, speed, and cooling under specified conditions.

Draft angles aid removal, while ejector pins push out the product. Distinguish gates from sprues and check each product/mold design. Manage rust, humidity, and dirt in storage; do not share a different product’s mold without authorization.

mfg1-electrical-l084.title: Board structure, exposure, development, and etching
mfg1-electrical-l084.exampleTitle: Removing film and copper are different stages
mfg1-electrical-l084.exampleText: The negative-resist concept here leaves exposed, hardened film, develops away unhardened film, etches exposed copper, then strips remaining protection. Do not describe needed protected copper as being removed along with it. Control temperature, concentration, cleaning, surface treatment, outline, and inspection conditions.
mfg1-electrical-l084.structureTitle: Layers and materials · Leave the needed conductors
mfg1-electrical-l084.structureText:
Single-, double-, and multilayer describe conductive-layer structure; rigid, flexible, and combined types describe form. Paper phenolic, glass epoxy, ceramics, and metal bases differ in substrate and thermal conditions. A board with mounted components is at a different manufacturing stage.

Subtractive formation creates a protective pattern over copper foil and etches unwanted copper. Another method selectively plates conductors. Mask pattern, exposure, and development depend on resist type; do not apply the same light/dark conditions to every process.

mfg1-mechanical-lesson-085.title: Identify lathe holding parts and feed-related components
mfg1-mechanical-lesson-085.exampleText: Part names help specify an abnormality’s location, but identifying a part does not authorize disassembly or adjustment. On a paper machine diagram, match the headstock, chuck, tool post, tailstock and carriage to their positions and roles. Ask the instructor about differences between actual machine models.
mfg1-mechanical-lesson-085.structureTitle: Target and role · Principles and distinctions
mfg1-mechanical-lesson-085.structureText:
The headstock relates to the spindle and other parts rotating the workpiece; the chuck grips the workpiece. The tailstock supports it from the opposite side and serves related purposes. The tool post holds the cutting tool, while the carriage, saddle and related parts move the tool. When learning names, use a diagram to distinguish which parts hold or move the workpiece or tool.

Soft jaws are relatively soft chuck jaws used to grip a workpiece, sometimes machined to fit it. Having chuck jaws does not mean every shape can be held safely. Fitting and jaw machining require appropriate training and approved methods. Do not check contact by hand during operation.

mfg1-mechanical-lesson-086.title: Compare the structures of milling machines, drill presses and machining centers
mfg1-mechanical-lesson-086.exampleText: When selecting a process, match the required face, tool-access direction, holding and equipment capability. Knowing part names in a drawing is separate from the training needed to move a table or change a tool in practice. Draw machining faces and tool directions on paper and practice reading the process sheet.
mfg1-mechanical-lesson-086.structureTitle: Target and role · Principles and distinctions
mfg1-mechanical-lesson-086.structureText:
A milling machine’s spindle-mounted tool rotates, machining through movement relative to the table carrying the workpiece and related parts. The bed and column support the machine; the spindle head and spindle relate to the tool side. For a drill press, organize the roles of the drill, chuck, column, table and base.

A machining center can change tools automatically. In the source’s examples, a vertical machine has a vertical spindle for operations such as top-face machining; a horizontal machine can use a rotary table and related arrangements to machine several faces without refixturing. The words vertical or horizontal alone do not prove that every part or face can be machined.

mfg1-mechanical-lesson-087.title: Organize grinding-wheel and chip hazards by process
mfg1-mechanical-lesson-087.exampleText: Welding involves intense light, heat, fumes and gases; casting involves hot molten metal and tools. In plastic working, a press shapes with force, forging uses blows and related forces, and rolling uses rolls. Match each process name with its hazards. One pair of gloves or protective glasses cannot be assumed to prevent every hazard.
mfg1-mechanical-lesson-087.structureTitle: Target and role · Principles and distinctions
mfg1-mechanical-lesson-087.structureText:
A grinder’s wheel rotates at high speed, and cracks or fractures can cause fragments to fly. Follow the specified training and procedures for pre-use inspection, fitting and trial runs. Appearance alone does not prove safety; ask the responsible person about uncertainty or abnormalities. Whether a wheel’s side may be used also depends on the tool’s specification.

Chips from lathes and similar machines are sharp and may be hot. After stopping and checking safety, clear them with the specified brush or other tool, not bare hands. Grinding removes material with abrasive grains; polishing uses paste-like abrasives and related materials to finish the surface. A shiny polished surface does not prove that hazardous chips or dimensional defects have disappeared.

mfg1-mechanical-lesson-088.title: Organize five resin-forming methods and solidification by process
mfg1-mechanical-lesson-088.exampleText: Materials that solidify by cooling and those that cure through reaction have different completion conditions. Producing a shape does not permit omitting cooling, curing, removal and inspection. Organize candidate methods from cross-section, material, how it solidifies and quantity. Actual temperature, pressure and composition follow approved instructions.
mfg1-mechanical-lesson-088.structureTitle: Target and role · Principles and distinctions
mfg1-mechanical-lesson-088.structureText:
Injection molding puts flowing resin into a mold. Blow molding introduces air into a tube-shaped or similar material to form a hollow shape against the mold. Extrusion continuously pushes material through a die to make long products of the same cross-section. A hollow tube is not necessarily blow-molded.

Compression molding presses material inside a mold; the source gives thermosetting resins, rubber and related examples. In the reinforced-plastic example, resin impregnates glass fibers or another reinforcement, rollers remove air, and a chemical reaction integrates the material. Reinforcement is not foreign matter to be removed wholesale.

mfg1-mechanical-lesson-089.title: Compare electrostatic painting and electrodeposition coating
mfg1-mechanical-lesson-089.exampleText: Connect the required functions—corrosion protection, appearance, insulation or heat shielding—to process requirements. Follow specified grounding, ventilation, suitable protection and other conditions for equipment using electricity and chemicals. Understanding the principle does not authorize changing bath conditions, supply or paint independently.
mfg1-mechanical-lesson-089.structureTitle: Target and role · Principles and distinctions
mfg1-mechanical-lesson-089.structureText:
Brushing or rolling paint across a surface differs from spraying atomized paint. Uniform-looking color does not by itself establish that either method meets requirements for the substrate, target face, thickness, drying and other conditions. Check the specified product and paint.

Electrostatic painting uses electrical force to attract charged paint particles to a product. The source explains product grounding and paint charging. Electrodeposition coating puts the product into a paint-containing bath and uses electricity to form the film. A bath process is different from attracting particles flying through space.

mfg1-mechanical-lesson-090.title: Compare hot and cold rolling through their benefits, constraints and later processes
mfg1-mechanical-lesson-090.exampleText: Rolling oil helps adjust friction, remove heat and suppress seizure or scratches. Check thickness, surface, strength and other requirements including later surface treatment and property adjustment. Not heating does not mean there is no roll-entanglement hazard or process heat. Check equipment and product conditions from the specified safe area.
mfg1-mechanical-lesson-090.structureTitle: Target and role · Principles and distinctions
mfg1-mechanical-lesson-090.structureText:
At high temperatures, hot-rolled material deforms more readily, with examples of substantial deformation using relatively less force. Cooling causes shrinkage, so dimensions and oxidation films formed by air reactions need checking. Consider heating energy too. Hot rolling does not make surface and dimensional checks unnecessary.

Cold rolling can provide dimensional accuracy and surface finish, but needs greater force and may cause work hardening. Check the process sheet for annealing and other post-treatment as needed. Confusing annealing with quenching changes the treatment’s purpose, so match the name and requirement.

mfg1-mechanical-lesson-091.title: Trace aluminum-extrusion processes and product features
mfg1-mechanical-lesson-091.exampleText: Die scratches, dirt and adhered metal, as well as debris on the runout table, are candidates when investigating lengthwise lines or surface scratches. Before-and-after inspections, cleaning and repair follow the responsible personnel’s procedure. Do not reach into a table while the machine moves or hold a hot product by hand to investigate a cause.
mfg1-mechanical-lesson-091.structureTitle: Target and role · Principles and distinctions
mfg1-mechanical-lesson-091.structureText:
Aluminum extrusion links billet heating, pushing through a die, cooling, straightening, cutting and related steps. The source gives a heating example around 400–500°C, not a workplace setpoint for every material. Too low a temperature can increase load; too high a temperature can cause cracks and other problems. Follow approved conditions combining material, shape and speed.

Examples include window sashes, door frames, structural members and heat-dissipation parts with fins. A sash may have a complex inner and outer shape. Fins increase surface area to help release heat. A continuing cross-section and satisfaction of required strength or surface quality are checked separately.

mfg1-electrical-l085.title: Connect specific hazards and signs to work
mfg1-electrical-l085.exampleText: No running, no mobile phones and no electronic devices are prohibition signs. Tsunami hazard zones differ from tsunami evacuation sites; rockfall and landslide warnings identify disaster types. Do not interchange flame, corrosion, health-hazard, aquatic-hazard and irritation information; match product identification to the SDS. A wide-area evacuation site may provide a broad space for refuge from major fires.
mfg1-electrical-l085.structureTitle: Safety devices and people nearby · Maintain visibility and clear routes
mfg1-electrical-l085.structureText:
Fixing one button of a two-hand machine frees a hand to enter the danger area. Distinguish removed guards, disabled sensors and third parties approaching an open rear side. Locate emergency stops before work; their presence does not justify omitting guards.

Loads blocking forward vision, open drains, stair cables and projections can cause collisions or falls. If a load hides your feet on stairs, do not proceed blindly; confirm an approved handling method. For solvent work, treat stopped ventilation, open containers and wet floors as separate hazards.

mfg1-electrical-l086.title: Read drawing requirements for paper, lines and lettering
mfg1-electrical-l086.exampleText: Example lettering heights are2.5,3.5,5,7 and10 mm. Avoid crossing dimension lines and duplicate dimensions; show finished sizes clearly. Arc length, chord length and central angle differ. Textbook process annotationsM andL indicate milling and turning and are read alongsideRa values. Check symbol editions and drawing legends.
mfg1-electrical-l086.structureTitle: Paper and borders · Widths and line types
mfg1-electrical-l086.structureText:
A0 is841×1189 mm;A1 594×841;A2 420×594;A3 297×420;A4 210×297. Textbook border examples use10 mm margins forA4–A2 and20 mm forA1 and larger. Check the adopted format and binding margin on the drawing; do not treat the paper edge itself as a dimensional reference.

The textbook’s basic thin/thick ratio is1:2, with examples0.18/0.35,0.25/0.5,0.35/0.7 and0.5/1.0 mm. Keep widths consistent for the same purpose in a drawing. Datum and pitch lines use chain lines; phantom lines for movement ranges may use double-chain lines; break boundaries use wavy or zigzag lines. Cutting-plane indications differ from section hatching.

mfg1-electrical-l087.title: Check electrical symbols against terminals and operation
mfg1-electrical-l087.exampleText: The textbook usesR for relays,MC for contactors,THR for thermal relays,BS for pushbuttons andL for lamps. Other diagrams may use different identifiers, so follow the legend. Distinguish ammetersA, fuses, circuit breakers and indicator lamps; follow functional relationships left-to-right horizontally or top-to-bottom vertically. Match coils and contacts by equipment number and location reference.
mfg1-electrical-l087.structureTitle: Symbol shape and function · Actuation and return
mfg1-electrical-l087.structureText:
Match resistor, variable-resistor, capacitor and coil symbols to their functions. For diodes,LEDs and photodiodes, checkA/K and whether light arrows are present and their direction. A pnp transistor hasB/C/E; its three connections are not interchangeable. A symbol is not a photograph of actual shape or terminal order.

Distinguish automatic return of pushbuttons or alarm switches from maintained emergency-stop actuation and manual release. Limit-switch symbols may indicate make, break or positive opening. Proximity and mechanical position switches also use different sensing principles. Similar names do not replace symbol/contact-behavior checks.

mfg1-electrical-l088.title: Use conditional comparisons of materials and insulation
mfg1-electrical-l088.exampleText: PET is thermoplastic, withMylar as an example name; phenolic and epoxy are thermosetting examples. Kraft paper and pressboard are insulation-paper examples; mica and ceramics are inorganic examples. The textbook explains temperature-rise limits by subtracting an ambient40°C from a maximum temperature, but this is not a universal product-use-limit formula. Also check temperature and reference water for specific-gravity comparisons.
mfg1-electrical-l088.structureTitle: Conductor comparison conditions · Magnetic and resistance materials
mfg1-electrical-l088.structureText:
The textbook compares aluminum conductivity at about60% of annealed copper and density at about one third. Low mass and good conduction are different advantages. Its20°C resistivity values are1/58 for annealed copper,1/55 for hard copper and1/35 for aluminum, used inΩ·mm²/m with area accounted for. Retain material and temperature assumptions; do not generalize to every alloy.

Nichrome and similar resistance materials exploit heating. Some materials minimize resistance changes with temperature; low resistance is not best for every use. Permeability and saturation flux density matter for cores; remanence and coercivity matter for permanent magnets. Compare ferrite and alnico by application requirements rather than one generic “magnetic strength.”

mfg1-electrical-l089.title: Match fastener shapes to tools
mfg1-electrical-l089.exampleText: Textbook mounting examples include holding the equipment-side screw head while tightening its nut, and fastening into tapped holes with machine screws. Different materials or receiving threads may change the assembly. Plastic/rubber washers and locking nuts also exist; matching photographs do not authorize substitution. Check part number, orientation, count and torque.
mfg1-electrical-l089.structureTitle: Tools turning the nut · Heads and washers
mfg1-electrical-l089.structureText:
A box driver, also called a nut driver, turns small nuts. Open-end and ring spanners must match the hex across-flats dimension; adjust an adjustable wrench without clearance. Check load direction against the movable-jaw construction and instructions, avoiding force that opens its jaws.

Machine screws include pan, countersunk and raised-countersunk heads; slotted and cross recesses require different tool fits. Washer-assembled screws are also calledSEMS screws. Flat washers spread load over the contact area and have specified positions, including metal/nonmetal combinations. Spring washers do not guarantee against loosening under every condition.

mfg1-electrical-l090.title: Check cutting-tool sequence and geometry to retain
mfg1-electrical-l090.exampleText: Lathes include headstock, chuck, toolpost, tailstock and feed mechanisms, combining workpiece rotation and tool feed. Milling uses relative motion between spindle tools and the table. Backlash is play affecting position after reversal. Check removal/compensation mechanisms and specifications; identical graduations do not always mean identical actual positions.
mfg1-electrical-l090.structureTitle: Holes and threads are separate operations · Tap and cutting-edge designs
mfg1-electrical-l090.structureText:
A textbook handworking example for a large square hole places spaced small holes inside the outline, cuts between them and files the remaining allowance. Do not cross the marked line; control workholding and sharp edges. General hole/chamfer examples are not universal machining instructions; follow part drawings and material.

Hand-tap sets may use first, intermediate and finishing taps in order. Choose for through/blind conditions and tool design; do not force an identical backing-off amount on every design. Drill flutes help remove chips. The textbook’s118° tip angle is representative, not universal for all materials. Distinguish brazed-tip and indexable turning tools.

mfg1-electrical-l091.title: Distinguish measurement principles from scale resolution
mfg1-electrical-l091.exampleText: LCR auto-balancing bridges use voltage, current and phase to obtain component values. Capacitance is the capacity to store charge between conductors; changes can detect thickness, displacement or liquid level. Distinguish the target quantity and electrical conversion; a capacitance change alone does not establish one unique cause.
mfg1-electrical-l091.structureTitle: Mechanism and minimum reading · Converting temperature and flux density
mfg1-electrical-l091.structureText:
The textbook micrometer advances0.5 mm per turn with50 thimble divisions, giving0.01 mm per division. Display resolution and accuracy differ. Some dial indicators read0.001 mm, but this is not every model; also check range, contact and management condition.

Thermocouples use thermoelectric voltage associated with temperature differences between junctions of two metals. The textbook’s typeK range is only an example; diameter, sheath, atmosphere and instrument change usable limits. In aHall element, a field perpendicular to current produces voltage perpendicular to both, a principle used in gaussmeters.

mfg1-electrical-l092.title: Compare passive-component construction and selection
mfg1-electrical-l092.exampleText: Lubrication supplies oil, grease or similar materials to reduce contact friction and wear. Grease consistency expresses softness, but penetration values andNLGI numbers run in opposite directions. Do not apply the textbook’s “larger values mean softer” statement to every grease grade number. Check standard, scale name and specified product.
mfg1-electrical-l092.structureTitle: Capacitor materials · Coils and functional elements
mfg1-electrical-l092.structureText:
Capacitors separate conductors with dielectric. In the textbook aluminum-electrolytic example, the anode is aluminum foil, the dielectric is aluminum oxide, and electrolyte also contributes to construction. Ceramic, film, multilayer-chip and variable types differ; even equal capacitance requires comparing polarity, temperature, frequency and aging conditions.

Coils may be wound, multilayer or thin-film; they are not always visibly wound around an iron core. Distinguish thermistor resistance/temperature behavior, piezoelectric force/electric conversion and quartz vibration. Diodes also serve detection, Zener-breakdown voltage control and photoelectric conversion besides rectification.

mfg1-electrical-l093.title: Explain fields and resistance circuits from equation conditions
mfg1-electrical-l093.exampleText: For two unloaded series resistors,V1=V0 R1/(R1+R2). For two parallel resistors,I1=I0 R2/(R1+R2), so a smallerR1 carries moreI1. Derive the opposite-branch numerator from shared voltage andI1=V/R1. Adding loads or meters changes the circuit, so the original ratio may no longer apply.
mfg1-electrical-l093.structureTitle: From charge to force · Graph slope
mfg1-electrical-l093.structureText:
Charge is measured inC; electric field relates to force per unit charge and differs from voltage or current. In the vacuum point-charge model, Coulomb force magnitude is|q1 q2|/(4πε0 r²). A changed medium changes the permittivity assumption; do not apply point-charge equations unconditionally to all nearby objects.

WithV horizontally andI vertically, straight-line slope isI/V=1/R. More current at the same voltage means lower resistance. Swapping axes changes slope meaning. Retain constant-temperature and other proportionality conditions; not every device has a straight-line characteristic.

mfg1-electrical-l094.title: Trace relays, contactors and overload detection together
mfg1-electrical-l094.exampleText: In a basic self-holding circuit, the relay’s own contact parallel to the start button maintains coil current, and stop conditions interrupt it. Ordinary electromagnetic relays lose energization on power loss. RetentivePLC settings and other restart circuits may behave differently; do not universally assume safe stopping after power restoration. Check actual circuits and restoration conditions.
mfg1-electrical-l094.structureText:
A contactor combined with a thermal overload relay is called a magnetic starter or magnetic switch. The contactor switches the load; the thermal relay detects overload and is not alone the main-circuit interrupter. Short-circuit protection is not necessarily the same function; check protection coordination.

Thermal operation responds to heating from current over time, so distinguish brief changes from sustained overload. Bimetal bends because two metals expand differently. After operation, check cause and safety and use approved reset procedures; do not repeatedly reset to keep running.
The protective purpose of this combination includes preventing a motor from burning out under overload. The textbook describes manual resetting of the signal, with safety checked first. For an actual device, verify the model specifications and approved procedure; this description alone is not a reason to change its reset settings.
Read the overload detection condition as both current at or above the set value and continuation for at least the specified duration. A bimetal is formed from two bonded metal plates with different thermal expansion rates.

mfg1-electrical-l095.title: Compare rotating machines and transformers by structure
mfg1-electrical-l095.exampleText: The textbook gives stray-load loss at roughly5–30% of copper loss as an example, not a fixed percentage for every transformer. Sulfur hexafluoride,SF6, is an insulation/cooling-gas example; check environmental impact and handling conditions. Vacuum/gas arc extinction differs in classification from oil-filled/molded insulation. Do not declare that no old oil breakers exist.
mfg1-electrical-l095.structureTitle: Rotors and starting conditions · Commands and detected values
mfg1-electrical-l095.structureText:
Three-phase induction machines include squirrel-cage and wound rotors. Star-delta current reduction assumes compatible three-phase windings compared at the same line voltage. Starting torque also changes; reduced current does not make it suitable for every load. Compare method, winding terminals, ratings, load and protection together.

Encoders encode rotation angles or linear displacement. Servos feed detected values back and correct command differences to control position, speed or torque. Distinguish feed-speed and winding-torque requirements; do not try to fix position error simply by increasing speed.

mfg1-electrical-l096.title: Separate structural, environmental and electrical tests
mfg1-electrical-l096.exampleText: Insulation resistance, withstand voltage, leakage and electromagnetic effects such asEMS require different methods. General labels like multimeter or oscilloscope do not establish suitability for all tests. Compare equipment, applied conditions, time, criteria and operator; identify nonconformities and connect them to records. Supplier inspection and finished-product evaluation do not unconditionally replace each other.
mfg1-electrical-l096.structureTitle: Structural checks · Sustained performance and external conditions
mfg1-electrical-l096.structureText:
Structural inspection checks size, weight, strength and assembly structure against requirements. Dimensions alone do not pass weight or strength. Appearance damage, function and structure have different purposes; compare the test sheet’s objects and methods.

Functional inspection checks required behavior for specified inputs; environmental testing applies prescribed temperature, humidity, vibration or shock. Accelerated-life tests use specified intensified conditions, not permission to raise temperature or voltage freely. Relating acceleration to normal lifetime involves evaluation assumptions.

mfg1-electrical-l097.title: Compare packaging materials and resin production conditions
mfg1-electrical-l097.exampleText: Blow molding inflates resin with air and differs from injection molding. Thermosets cross-link and cannot be remelted in the same way. Biodegradability depends on conditions and does not permit abandonment anywhere. FRP can use impregnation, lay-up and pressure; it is not all made exclusively by high-temperature, high-pressure pressing.
mfg1-electrical-l097.structureTitle: Materials and logistics requirements · Volume production and tooling cost
mfg1-electrical-l097.structureText:
Match paperboard boxes, corrugated packaging, wooden boxes and metal/glass/plastic containers to products, transport and storage. Square or nearly square timber is one material example; required restraint strength comes from packaging design. Prioritize protection and efficiency over decoration; minimum material does not justify omitting necessary cushioning or restraint.

Injection molding suits making many identical shapes quickly, but precision molds have initial costs and are not always cheapest for small batches. Screw feeding, holding pressure, cooling and shrinkage are distinct conditions. Do not universally determine injection quantity from rotation speed alone; check metering/injection mechanisms and standards.

mfg1-electrical-l098.title: Distinguish PCB stages and machining scales
mfg1-electrical-l098.exampleText: Wet etching chemically removes unwanted copper with solutions, unlike mechanical polishing. Control solution concentration, temperature and washing. The textbook compares submillimeter PCB scales with nanometer semiconductor scales, not a single line width for every product.1 mm=10⁶nm; verify the order-of-magnitude conversion.
mfg1-electrical-l098.structureTitle: Board roles and heat dissipation · Process sequence
mfg1-electrical-l098.structureText:
A motherboard is a main board connectingCPU, memory and other items. Metal-base boards combine metal, insulation and copper conductors to aid heat dissipation; a metal base does not permit direct electrical continuity between patterns and the metal plate. Distinguish single/double/multilayer structure from application names.

A conceptual subtractive copper-clad-board flow includes cutting, drilling/copper plating, photosensitive film, exposure/development and etching. Solder resist, legend printing, surface finishing, outline machining/V-cutting and inspection have separate roles; verify actual sequence against process instructions. Do not confuse circuit-forming film with solder resist on the finished board.
